title: Telemetry-friendly JSON schema format and fault ID guidance for tool calls
creator: Sofia Lopez
description: Define a compact, telemetry-friendly JSON schema authoring format and a stable fault ID scheme for tool/function calling. The goal is to make runtime validation results machine-actionable (for routing & automated fallbacks) and developer-friendly (clear remediation hints in SDKs). This ticket covers schema authoring conventions, runtime validator behavior, error taxonomy, and mapping to telemetry/fault IDs that are consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Deliverables: a normative spec doc, a validation library update, and a runtime telemetry mapping table.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document (Confluence) describing the JSON schema authoring constraints and recommended annotations is published
Runtime validator library accepts new annotations and emits structured failure objects with stable fault IDs
SDKs display human-friendly error text plus the fault ID, and actionable remediation hints when available
Telemetry pipeline ingests fault IDs and we have dashboard + alert for high-rate customer-facing faults
Backward compatibility: existing simple schemas continue to work without modification
design_notes: Favor a small set of schema annotations: required, type, enum, pattern, range, examples, intent_hint, severity_hint
Introduce optional 'shapeVersion' annotation to allow progressive schema evolution without breaking runtime validators
Fault ID format: RF:<category>:<shortcode>:v<major> e.g. RF:PARAM:TYPE_MISMATCH:v1 — compact, parseable, and suitable for telemetry indexes
Emit both machine and human fields in validation result: {fault_id, category, path, human_message, suggestion, severity}
Edge cases: streaming partial failures should surface as 'soft' faults with 'severity_hint: low' so callers can choose to continue
implementation_plan: Write spec doc and example schemas (Confluence) — owner: Sofia
Extend runtime validator to recognize new annotations and produce structured faults — owner: Ravi
Add mapping layer that converts structured faults to compact fault IDs and tags for telemetry ingestion — owner: Infra
Update JS/Python SDK error wrapper to show human_message and provide quick-fix links — owner: DevX
Create dashboard: fault rates by fault_id + customer_id threshold alert — owner: Observability
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting held with Product/Design/Infra. Agreed on scope and non-goals (no schema DSL rewrite).
2026-03-05: Draft of spec posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TOOL/Telemetry+Friendly+Schema — initial review requested
2026-03-09: Prototype validator emits structured fault object locally; sample fault ID format RF:PARAM:ENUM_MISMATCH:v1
2026-03-12: Discussed trade-off between long descriptive fault IDs vs compact codes. Chose compact format for telemetry efficiency; human_message carries full text
2026-03-14: Implemented telemetry mapping table and created initial Grafana panel (infra PR #482).
review_feedback: PM (Michael Chen): prioritize providing remediation hints for P0/P1 faults so customers can self-remediate quickly
Design (Aisha Patel): error UX should avoid jargon; prefer examples and next-step buttons in Console
Security (Helen Wu): validate that schema annotations cannot be abused to leak PII — agreed to sanitize example fields before ingest
Infra (Diego Ramos): ensure fault IDs are fixed-length tokens in telemetry to avoid ingestion cardinality explosion
test_plan: Unit tests: validator produces expected fault objects for malformed inputs
Integration tests: SDK surfaces fault ID + human_message; Console links to docs
E2E: simulate large-scale invalid-parameter traffic and verify telemetry pipeline aggregates by fault_id
Backward compatibility tests: validate old schemas pass through with no additional annotations required
rollback_plan: Remove telemetry mapping and revert validator changes if production telemetry shows >5x spike in cardinality or critical false positives. Deploy a feature flag to toggle new annotations at runtime for Private deployments.
risk_assessment: Medium. Main risks: increased telemetry cardinality, unclear error text causing support tickets, and accidental exposing of example values containing sensitive data. Mitigations: compact fault IDs, UX review, sanitize example fields before logging.
estimated_cost_savings: Expected 6-8% reduction in support TTR and 3% token-cost reduction for common rerun flows due to better client-side validation
